current_evidence: The council's 'What do I need to submit?' guidance page (planning-applications-guidance/planning-7/2) links to downloads/file/4686 and says the checklist was 'updated and adopted on 5 December 2024' replacing the January 2023 version; no newer 2025/2026 version or open consultation was found.

issues.detail: The List date is recorded as 2024-12-01, but the document and the guidance page both give the adoption date as 05 December 2024. Grokbot's own 'Date basis' note also says 5 December.

Grokbot also read the superseded Draft Planning Validation Checklist 2022 (downloads/file/4495) and took requirements from it, mixing them in with the current list: Block plan, Design and Access Statement, Landscaping proposals (Core Strategy CG1.1 etc.), Schedule of works (listed building), Telecoms ICNIRP statement, Structural survey, the Outline ecological assessment row, and the Contaminated Land and Open Space rows. The 'Planning page' field also points to that 2022 draft consultation page rather than the current guidance page.
issues.evidence: Planning page https://www.bolton.gov.uk/directory-record/3383/planning-validation-checklist = 'Draft Planning Validation Checklist', consultation closed 12 October 2022

issues.detail: Householder is recorded as '(none)', but the 2024 list applies several items to house extensions. These are: Heritage Statement (all development including house extensions in a Conservation Area or affecting the setting of a heritage asset); Tree Surveys (house extensions where trees with a stem over 75 mm are within the site or within 10 m of the red line, or hedges are on site); Levels/Sections (house extensions, except rear terraced extensions up to 4 m or where the level change is no more than 1 m within 21 m); and House Extension Justification.
issues.evidence: Item 33 Tree Surveys: 'All development including house extensions where trees within the site or within 10 m of the red line...'; Item 15 Heritage Statement: 'All development (including house extensions and demolition) in a Conservation Area'

issues.detail: The Listed building consent rows are 'Landscaping scheme' (put there only because the text mentions the setting of a Listed Building) and 'Structural Survey' (from the 2022 draft). They miss the Heritage Statement, which the 2024 list requires for ALL Listed Building Consent applications, and the Archaeological Assessment for works within a listed building's curtilage.
issues.evidence: Item 15 Heritage Statement: 'all Listed Building Consent applications'

issues.detail: Contaminated Land and 'Open space / play space assessment' are placed under 'Minerals & waste (county)'. Bolton is a metropolitan borough, and both rows come from the 2022 draft. The 'Open space' excerpt is actually contaminated-land text about sensitive uses such as schools, play areas and allotments. In the current list, Open Space (Needs & Opportunities Assessment) applies to Major and Minor schemes that cause loss of open space or sports land.
issues.evidence: Item 22: 'Major and Minor causing loss or partial loss of open space or sports/recreation land or buildings'

issues.detail: 41 rows are marked 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning'. The 2024 list expresses most triggers as 'Major' and/or 'Minor' development, which also covers outline applications, and some items exclude house extensions explicitly. Examples: BNG (all Major and Minor unless exempt), Planning Statement (all Major), SuDS (all Major; Minor of 5+ dwellings or 500 sqm+). Outline has only one row, taken from the 2022 draft.
issues.evidence: Item 4 BNG: 'All Major and Minor, unless exempt'; Item 24 Planning Statement: 'All Major; departures from the Development Plan'

issues.detail: Three items in the 2024 list were not captured at all: (1) Green Belt Justification (new), required for all development in the Green Belt; (2) Public Art, required for Major schemes on sites of 1 ha+, Major schemes over 2,500 sqm, or Major schemes of 50+ dwellings; (3) House Extension Justification (new), required for house extensions solely for a disabled person's benefit that would not normally be acceptable.
issues.evidence: Summary table items 13 (Green Belt Justification), 25 (Public Art), 16 (House Extension Justification)

issues.detail: Many triggers are navigation fragments or policy prose rather than the 'When required' criteria. BNG, Crime, Ecology, EIA, Noise and LVIA read 'To Table X When Required'. Contaminated Land and Heritage quote policy aims. Retail/Town Centre quotes the NPPF sequential principle instead of the local thresholds (sequential assessment for main town centre uses over 250 sqm outside allocated shopping areas; impact assessment over 2,500 sqm). Many others start mid-sentence with 'above, an X will be required', so the criteria are lost (Air Quality, Coal Mining, Fire, FRA, SuDS, HIA, Lighting).
issues.evidence: Item 31: 'Sequential: main town centre uses over 250 sqm outside allocated shopping areas. Impact: retail or leisure over 2,500 sqm'

issues.detail: Several requirement rows are not items in the 2024 list. 'Statement of Community Involvement' is just a link title followed by the 'Public Art When Required' heading. 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' is advice text. 'Agricultural Land Classification / Soils' is Places for Everyone policy prose. 'Construction (Environmental) Management Plan' is 'to submit construction management plans as appropriate'. 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage' quotes the Health Impact Assessment criteria about waste management and minerals.
issues.evidence: SCI excerpt: 'Bolton Council – Statement of Community Involvement Back To Table Public Art When Required'

issues.detail: The tab items include fragments and process text from the 2022 draft: 'How to read, write and use them (CABE) ign-and-access-statements.pdf 7 Environmental Statement...', 'Surface water drainage works ... 17 Systems (March 2015): 5773/sustainable-drainage-technical-standards.pdf', and 'However, if there is no justification ... the application is likely to be returned to you.'
issues.evidence: tab_items 'Submission rules' section, sources file/4495 and file/4686

issues.detail: Telecommunications is placed under 'Change of use - prior approval'. The source covers Part 24 telecoms prior notification, which is not a change-of-use prior approval, and its excerpt still cites the GPDO 1995 wording.
issues.evidence: Item 30: 'All telecoms proposals, including Part 24 prior notification applications'

summary: Grokbot's link is the current Bolton Local Validation Checklist 2024+ (adopted 5 Dec 2024), though the date is recorded as 1 Dec. The extraction mixes in the superseded 2022 draft. It wrongly shows no householder or LBC-specific requirements, misses the Green Belt Justification, Public Art and House Extension Justification items, and many triggers are navigation fragments or policy prose.
